rationale: There is clear evidence that the NFU1 phenotypic spectrum forms a continuum where hypomorphic missense variants can produce milder, juvenile/adult or slowly progressive hereditary spastic paraplegia (SPG93, OMIM #620938) rather than rapid, fatal infantile multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 1 (MMDS1). However, the hypothesis fails on two critical assertions: first, c.565G>A (p.Gly189Arg) is classically documented in severe, infantile-onset MMDS1 cases rather than being exclusively restricted to or diagnostic of non-lethal SPG93; second, other distinct missense variants (e.g., p.Leu99Val [c.295C>G] and p.Val241Leu) cause SPG93, directly disproving the claim that specific recurrent alleles such as c.565G>A and c.332G>T account for 100% of non-lethal HSP presentations.

conflicts: The hypothesis posits that specific hypomorphic alleles such as c.565G>A (p.Gly189Arg) account for non-lethal pediatric/adolescent HSP presentations, but literature (Ahting et al. 2015, Wesley et al. 2017) shows p.Gly189Arg is a recognized pathogenic mutation underlying severe infantile MMDS1.

The claim that these specific alleles account for 100% of non-lethal HSP presentations is disproved by the identification of other independent pathogenic missense alleles in SPG93, including c.295C>G (p.Leu99Val) and p.Val241Leu.

new_directions.question_text: What residual [4Fe-4S] cluster transfer activity threshold separates fatal infantile MMDS1 from surviving SPG93 phenotypes across documented NFU1 missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: Quantifying in vitro cluster transfer and stability across p.Leu99Val, p.Val241Leu, p.Gly189Arg, and c.332G>T will elucidate the biochemical cut-off for clinical spastic paraplegia versus multisystem metabolic collapse.

new_directions.question_text: Do modifying alleles or intragenic compound heterozygosity explain why p.Gly189Arg manifests as severe MMDS1 in some pedigrees but milder neurological presentations in others?
new_directions.rationale: Resolving discrepancies in clinical severity for identical alleles will determine whether clinical SPG93 classification requires second-site epistatic modifiers or tissue-specific residual expression.
